text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

In our daily report of March 4 it was emphasized that in spite of the overall tight supply situation, the market seems to be due for a technical correction. However, the following day prices continued to surge ahead but the awaited correction set in on March 6.

But in spite of the setback today, we may not have seen the peak yet. March gave up $40 to close at $1,745 per tonne, while May ended $45 lower at $1,735. Arabica futures in New York closed lower across the board with front month March losing 7.80 cents/lb to close at 211.95 cents/lb, while May gave up 6.95 cents/lb to close at 193.70 cents/lb.

Apart from profit taking talk Colombia would open registrations for April/June coffee shipments may have exaccerbated the slide. After the close of trading, Colombian coffee officials confirmed April/June registrations for private exporters would be opened on Friday, March 7.

In addition to the 1.07 million bags of new excelso coffee it authorized for shipment the National Growers Federation indicated it might approve the sale of 300,000 bags of old coffee during the same period. However, the tight supply situation is likely to hold and probably the market has only paused before moving up further.

But some switching of blends seems to be occurring given the wide disparity between New York and London robusta and this too might be taking some of the sting out of the market, at least temporarily, traders said. Given the current volatility it is difficult to predict which way the market will go but current fundamentals suggest that it will be a very interesting year.

BRAZIL - Some analysts doubted that Brazil will be able to meet a 6 million bag export quota set by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) in January to June 1997 but the current rate of exports suggests that this will be easily achieved and possibly even exceeded.

Coffee shipments are now expected to be in excess of 1 million 60-kg bags and could even exceed January's 1.25 million bags despite the shorter working month and the carnival holidays. As of February 4, bills of lading totalled 1.05 million bags while 1.32 million bags had been registered for shipment, according to a report by the Santos export firm Icatu/Sumatra.

The question now is how big the crop in 1996/97 will be. Most estimates are in the region of 27 million bags although some estimate the crop at 28 million bags and even beyond. The question arises whether larger than expected Brazilian exports could bring prices down.

COLOMBIA - The National Coffee Growers Federation said it was opening registrations for April/June shipments by private exporters as of Friday, March 7. The Federation said private exporters had been authorized to ship up to 1.071 million 60- kg bags of fresh excelso coffee during the three-month period.

But it added that there was the possibility that private exporters would also be authorized to ship an additional 300,000 bags of old coffee from existing inventories. Federation shipments for April have been set at 243,428 70-kg bags of fresh coffee and 50,000 bags from earlier crops in Federation stockpiles, official sources said.

NETHERLANDS - The Netherlands imported 327,173 bags of coffee in October 1996, 20 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 2.656 million bags, 9.6 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995.

Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 1.8 per cent to 2.910 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Uganda (153,100 vs 177,900 bags), El Salvador (184,500 vs 78,900 bags), Brazil (107,100 vs 308,800 bags) and Colombia (374,800 vs 357,000 bags).

The country exported 474,000 bags of coffee in January/October 1996, 8 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 15 per cent to 616,900 bags.
